strings.name: Philippe Starck
strings.summary: Starck moved from furniture and interiors into hotels, household goods and varied consumer products. Working with Alessi, Kartell and hotel developers, he expanded design’s public visibility through Juicy Salif, Louis Ghost and shared spaces. His “democratic design” ideal coexists with luxury projects; form, function and consumer culture provide important perspectives on his work. He received the 2026 DesignEuropa Lifetime Achievement Award.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Brought design language into everyday consumption through furniture, product and spatial design, influencing public understanding of industrial design and lifestyles.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Everyday objects and visual language
strings.highlights.h1.text: Worked with brands to introduce sculptural form, humor and new materials into furniture and household products.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended the Camondo school in Paris.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Design and everyday spaces
strings.highlights.h2.text: Restaurant and hotel projects combined spatial experience with objects, extending design’s influence in daily consumption.
strings.timeline.t1.title: DesignEuropa lifetime award
strings.timeline.t1.text: Received lifetime recognition in the EU Intellectual Property Office’s design awards.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Louis Ghost chair
strings.timeline.t2.text: Launched a transparent plastic armchair with Kartell, recasting classical furniture forms in industrial material.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Juicy Salif lemon squeezer
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Alessi cast-aluminum squeezer became a signature product, combining utensil and sculptural appearance.
strings.timeline.t4.title: New York Royalton hotel
strings.timeline.t4.text: Designed interiors for Ian Schrager’s hotel, contributing to the development of boutique hotels.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Paris Café Costes
strings.timeline.t5.text: Designed the café’s space and furniture, attracting wider attention to his work.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Élysée private rooms
strings.timeline.t6.text: Designed interiors for the French presidential residence, gaining a major public commission.
strings.timeline.t7.title: La Main Bleue nightclub
strings.timeline.t7.text: Designed the Montreuil nightclub’s interior, developing his early spatial practice.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Inflatable-object enterprise
strings.timeline.t8.text: Established an inflatable-object business, exploring lightweight materials and objects for living.
